title: Fixed temp filenames make concurrent config/auth saves race-prone
reasoning: Both persistence helpers write to a deterministic temp path ending in .tmp and then rename it into place. If two async saves overlap, one call can overwrite the other's temp file before rename, or the second rename can fail after the first has already moved the shared temp file. That can lose the newer payload or report a failed save even though callers provided valid state.
recommendation: Serialize writes per target file or use unique temp filenames per write followed by atomic rename. If last-writer-wins is intended, enforce that ordering explicitly with a small write queue.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No included tests exercise overlapping calls to the save helpers or assert deterministic last-writer-wins behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests that start two concurrent saves with different payloads and assert both promises settle predictably and the final file contains the intended last payload.
minimumFixScope: saveFrontendConfigToDisk, saveInstallAuthStateToDisk, and focused persistence concurrency tests.
